newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo credit assn says unrecoverable loans Y24 bln.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo credit assn says unrecoverable loans Y24 bln.

text.p: Tokyo-based Musashino Shinkin Bank, a small deposit-taking financial firm, faces financial problems with unrecoverable loans totalling 24.2 billion yen and has given up efforts to restructure on its own, a bank official said on Monday.
The official told Reuters that the credit association had asked an industry group for financial support.
Musashino would not confirm a Japanese newspaper report that said it was seeking a merger with Tokyo-based Johnan Shinkin Bank, the nation's largest credit association.

Mass circulation Japanese daily Asahi Shimbun said in a report on Monday that Musashino Shinkin had collapsed under the weight of massive non-performing loans and was now seeking a merger with Johnan Shinkin Bank.
Despite the report, there was neither chaos at the association nor a run on deposits, the bank official said.

An official at Johnan Shinkin Bank confirmed that the bank had received an offer to absorb the troubled Musashino Shinkin from an industry group, but added that the offer failed to meet Johnan's requirements. "At the moment... Nothing has been decided yet," the official said.

Separately, a senior Finance Ministry official told reporters that final discussions were now under way on how to deal with Musashino Shinkin, but added that no decision had yet been made on whether it would be able to merge with Johnan Shinkin.
"I have not received any detailed report yet. Final discussions are now under way over how to deal with the (financial) problem," the ministry official said when asked about the Asahi report.
